coverage.DOM-001: The kernel creates immutable Agent revisions and preserves the selected revision after a later Agent revision; the state compiler/planner test exercises receipt-bound revision registration.
coverage.DOM-002: The kernel creates a Session from a resolved revision and preserves the original revision pin across later Agent revisions and repeated inspection.
coverage.DOM-004: Kernel Input tests cover canonical idempotent admission and bounded/invalid content refusal. The disposable PostgreSQL admission run verifies reference-only storage, replay, concurrent distinct Input admission, and pre-staging Artifact authorization denial.
coverage.DOM-005: Kernel completion/cancellation race and state planner settlement tests prove one terminal Turn outcome and promotion only after the winning settlement.
coverage.DOM-006: The kernel proves ordered one-active admission under 24 concurrent Inputs; the disposable PostgreSQL admission test independently proves concurrent distinct Inputs persist as distinct queued Turns behind the active Turn.
coverage.DOM-007: The state planner proves a retryable failure retains the running Turn and a retry creates a distinct next ordinal/fence invocation within that same Turn. The model worker invokes a fresh intent once, reconciles an expired claim by its exact operation ID without reinvocation, and records an uncertain provider outcome safely. Disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO tests additionally prove producer-loss replay and normalized-output finalization.
coverage.DOM-008: The state planner persists a Tool intent and approval decision before creating execution work. The durable tool lifecycle proves the authorized descriptor/approval/grant path; corrupt or missing descriptors are refused before adapter execution.
coverage.DOM-009: Planner and public StateRuntime tests cover bounded grant owner/scope, expiry, maximum use, policy digest, idempotent audit facts, and refusal before execution. Public projections exclude capability bytes and descriptors.
coverage.DOM-010: The planner persists Conversation content only by immutable reference, enforces expected-version conflict, and returns the original result on exact replay.
coverage.DOM-011: Artifact registration retains ID/media type/size/digest metadata with authorization/audit/outbox effects. Disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO tests prove authorized input/readback and reject forged or cross-principal references.
coverage.DOM-012: Public HTTP/SDK inspection returns the stable safe unavailable Failure code/message/retryability while the model worker retains uncertainty rather than leaking provider diagnostics.
coverage.DOM-013: Public HTTP/SDK inspection keeps an absent output token count unknown rather than zero. The disposable normalized HTTP fixture persists and exposes provider-neutral input/output usage with the owner-readable immutable output Artifact.

limitations: DOM-003 remains unpromoted: SessionCancelled and SessionFailed are public enum values, but the current state planner/kernel evidence implements and tests only open, closing, and completed Session transitions.

The normalized HTTP endpoint is a local protocol fixture using disposable PostgreSQL and MinIO; it is not a supported external model-provider, deployed model-role, credential-source, or live-provider claim.
Tool evidence proves the durable authorization/control-plane lifecycle only. It does not execute an external sandbox command.
The disposable dependencies are not protected production operations and this evidence makes no Firecracker, Linux KVM, release-tag, or external-consumer claim.
